runs.content:
## New investigation idea

- **[2026-10-01] Today's podcast recommendation names a 2026 book, *Messy Jobs*, as a direct argument against AI-driven mass unemployment. Its authorship is muddled in the suggestion text, and nothing in Books or AI & Tech has it.** [[podcasts/suggestions]] (week of 2026-10-01, Conversations with Tyler) first calls *Messy Jobs* "his" (Tyler Cowen's) 2026 book, then says the Luis Garicano episodes (Jul 28 and Aug 27, 2026) are the ones that cover it. So it is unclear who wrote it. The thesis is that AI makes jobs messier rather than eliminating them. That is the book-length counter-position [[ai-tech/ai-future-of-work]] lacks. Its existing feeders (BofA reskilling, the Gates robot tax, Exponential View) all cover policy or retraining, not whether the job loss happens at all. **Action:** (1) Confirm the author and year with one web search before the name spreads to other pages under the wrong author. (2) If it checks out, add it to [[books/suggestions]] or the reading list as the AI-work counterweight. (3) Use the Garicano episode as the source for a "jobs get messier, not fewer" counter-argument section in ai-future-of-work. Note: ai-future-of-work now has 5+ open feeder ideas in this file and none actioned, so it may be worth one consolidated update rather than another ingest.

## New cross-domain connection

- **[2026-10-01] Today's Circle Round recommendation is a finished, professionally produced example of the two things Lightfin's own pages are still designing on paper: an interactive listener beat inside a children's audio episode, and a fable turned into a short radio play.** [[podcasts/suggestions]] (week of 2026-10-01) pitches WBUR's Circle Round as craft study for Lightfin: folktales adapted into 15–25 minute full-cast audio dramas. Its spin-off *The Midnight Rebellion* ends each episode with a choice for the listener. [[lightfin/story-bible]] already builds an interactive device into every episode, the "15-second mystery pause" ("Can you guess who did it?") before the reveal. Circle Round is the nearest real-world test of whether a participation beat holds young listeners in pure audio, and of where it goes (mid-episode pause vs end-of-episode choice). Separately, [[lightfin/story-little-ninja]] describes itself as "more fable than adventure" and possible "as a short audio piece". Circle Round's format (one fable, about 20 minutes, music plus a cast) is the ready template for that adaptation. Neither Lightfin page cites any produced comparator for these devices. The previous audio-craft suggestions (Scriptnotes 07-16, Sound School 09-03) teach the techniques; this one is the first that shows the finished product.
